title: load_threaded_request -  issues with relative paths that point to the same resource
body:
### Tested versions

Cusotm-Build based on tagged branch "[4.7.2-stable](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/releases/tag/4.7.2-stable)"



### System information

Godot v4.7.2.rc (7160efa07) - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA RTX 3500 Ada Generation Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9671) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-13950HX (32 threads) - 63.69 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

The issue is related to calling `ResourceLoader::load_threaded_request` using relative paths that point to the same resource. 

Example Situation: 
- Real Path: res://Art/Explosion_01.png
- Relative Path A: res:://Actor/BigExplosion/../../Art/Explosion_01.png
- Relative Path B: res:://Actor/Ninja/Disappear/../../../Art/Explosion_01.png

If I typed them correct, both relative paths point to the same `Explosion_01.png` resource. 

You can call into `ResourceLoader::load_threaded_request` with both relative paths, and the system returns an `Error::OK` for both calls. Calls into `ResourceLoader::load_threaded_get_status` also properly track the "load" progress of both relative paths. 

However, calling `ResourceLoader::load_threaded_get` on both relative paths can cause issues.

When building Godot i ndebug mode, the above can reliably cause a `DEV_ASSERT` to be hit at line 950 of `resource_loader.cpp` (inside `ResourceLoader::load_threaded_get`)

When running the Godot editor in release mode, this can "sometimes" result in the 2nd call to `ResourceLoader::load_threaded_get` to return a null resource instead of the successfully loaded resource. 

#### Our Investigation: 
From our own investigation, inside `ResourceLoader::_load_start`, the 2 different relative paths are both being given their own `LoadToken` with `LoadToken::user_rc = 1`. 

Then, when the loading is complete and ResourceLoader::load_threaded_get is called twice, but upon the second call, the `LoadToken::user_rc == 0`, hitting the dev assert and, likely, causing the return resource to be null sometimes.

#### Our Workaround
We have found that resolving relative paths before we call `ResourceLoader::load_threaded_get` (using `String::simplify_path`) prevents the issue. 

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have a resource in the project folder
2. Call `ResourceLoader::load_threaded_request` with a relative path to the resource (`RelPathA`)
3. Call `ResourceLoader::load_threaded_request` with a "different" relative path to the resource (`RelPathB`)
4. Wait for `ResourceLoader::load_threaded_get_status` to return that both paths are loaded
5. Call `ResourceLoader::load_threaded_get` with `RelPathA`
6. Call `ResourceLoader::load_threaded_get` with `RelPathB`

If in a debug build, observe the DEV_ASSERT being hit
If in a release build, notice that sometimes the call to `ResourceLoader::load_threaded_get` with `RelPathB` will return a null resource. 

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A
